title: The CSP allows no inline code but the landing's head script by hash; astro.config.mjs forbids inlining scripts — keep it that way
body:
public/_headers sends script-src 'self' + the two analytics hosts + ONE sha256: the landing's head script (LANDING_HEAD_SCRIPT in src/lib/landing-head.ts). Any other inline code is blocked in production only (astro preview and dist/ carry no CSP).
1) Astro inlines a page script whose chunk is under vite.build.assetsInlineLimit. It bit twice on 2026-10-29: Analytics.astro's startAnalytics(), then the brief view's reveal once its canvas code was removed. astro.config.mjs now sets assetsInlineLimit to a function that returns false for .js (everything else keeps Vite's default, so small font subsets still inline as data:). Do not remove or loosen it; `pnpm run test:js` rejects inline executable scripts as the backstop.
2) Editing LANDING_HEAD_SCRIPT changes its sha256: put the new hash in public/_headers in the same diff (test:js recomputes it; test:served checks the served policy after deploy). Keep the script constant: the build id lives in <meta name="build-id">. Never fix a blocked script with 'unsafe-inline'.
not_derivable: The CSP only exists once Cloudflare serves _headers, so the breakage is invisible locally; that Astro inlines small scripts is framework behaviour, not visible in the source.
